From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Lingual suitability summary + action plan for EU & APAC locales

Hi Aiko, Lena — thanks again for the demo this morning. High-level recap and proposed next steps based on what we discussed: 

What we tested today
- Demo used rdx-7b-q4f (quantized) and rdx-14b-pt (float16) on a mixed JA/EN + DE test set you provided.
- Quick regen checks on JA tone and DE formal/neutral splits.

Preliminary recommendations
- For JA-centric flows: rdx-14b-pt for correctness-sensitive responses; rdx-7b-q4f for chat-like interactive UIs (lower cost).
- For DE/FR/EU languages: rdx-7b-q4f with recommended tokenizer tweaks (see README in attached csv).
- For low-resource APAC languages (TH, VI): we recommend targeted fine-tune or a narrow evaluation before rollout — risk of hallucination noted.

Deliverables I attached
- locales-benchmark-summary.csv (quick metrics: accuracy, BLEU-ish proxies, safety flags)
- prompt-sets_v1.zip (sample prompts we used for JA / DE / EN mix)

Open questions / asks from your side
1) Prioritize three target locales for the PoC (we need to know which to run deeper evals on).
2) Confirm acceptance criteria (latency SLO / accuracy thresholds / example prompts).
3) Procurement timing — do you need an SOW or is PO sufficient to start dedicated benchmarking?

Proposed timeline
- This week: sign off on target locales + accept criteria.
- Next week: focused eval run (2 days) for prioritized locales, deliver refined prompt sets + evaluation dashboard.
- Week after: optional canary rollout on a small subset of traffic.

I'll loop in Marissa to outline the technical runbook and Monica for commercial items. If you'd like a short readout call Friday (30 mins) we can go over the benchmarks live.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Aditya — very clear summary. A few items from our side: 

- Priority locales: JA (high), EN (product docs), DE (customer support). Secondary: TH, VI (exploratory).
- On Japanese: tone adaptation is critical — we need conservative politeness levels for outbound messages (no casual forms). Can you provide sample prompts that bias for polite/formal JA?
- Procurement: we prefer an SOW + milestone invoice schedule. Procurement will need estimated run hours for evaluation and a sample SOW to review.

Also: are you seeing any tokenization-related regressions with JA/EN code-mixed inputs? We had a data point where code-switching affected entity recognition in a previous PoC.

If you can send the sample JA prompts and a suggested SOW draft, procurement will start review. Friday readout works for us — 09:00 JST preferred.

Best,
Aiko
Aiko Tanaka
Head of AI Integration | KuroTech
aiko.tanaka@kurotech.jp

Hi all — quick technical clarifications and proposed small experiments we can run as part of the focused eval: 

1) JA polite/formal prompts: attached ja-en-prompt-examples.md contains three prompt templates that push for keigo avoidance and polite desu/masu endings. We also include examples that preserve English acronyms unchanged.
2) Tokenization / code-switching: we observed a drop in NER recall when English entity tokens are embedded inline with Japanese (example in the CSV). Workaround: use explicit entity anchors in the prompt ("[ENT]...") or run a short pre-tokenization pass to normalize mixed script segments. We'll include a small preproc script if you want it as part of the PoC.
3) TH/VI risk: model perplexity and hallucination rate spike on sparse vocab. For those locales, we recommend: (a) narrow eval with 500 doc prompts, (b) optional lightweight fine-tune on customer-provided in-domain examples.

Runbook + timing
- We can deliver the focused eval for prioritized three locales within 48 hours once you sign off and provide final sample corpus (3k tokens per language min).
- Deliverables: per-locale precision/recall proxies, example failure cases, recommended prompt set, and a short SLO doc.

I've attached ja-en-prompt-examples.md and will push the preproc script to the drive folder linked below.

-Marissa Cole
Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment stubs: ja-en-prompt-examples.md (text)
